supervisor_assignments.name: supervisor_assignments
supervisor_assignments.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- assignment id: use the subject-person table primary key as the assignment identifier
  sp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS assignment_id,
  -- activity id: link to subject_detail via the subject_person key to carry exact stored activity identifier
  sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS activity_id,
  -- person id and name and role from subject_person table (exact columns preserved)
  sp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS person_id,
  sp.PERSON_NAME AS person_name,
  sp.PERSON_ROLE AS person_role
FROM iap_subject_person AS sp
-- join to subject_detail so each person assignment that is linked to an activity is represented with that activity id.
-- We keep all person rows that have a matching subject_detail row; if you need persons without activities, remove the JOIN or make it LEFT JOIN.
JOIN iap_subject_detail AS sd
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
supervisor_assignments.description: Select person-role assignments (supervisors) including assignment id, person id, person name, and person role for roles that may be linked to activities. Do not filter by role here (role filter applied in final step), but keep one row per assignment.

unique_title_leader_rows.name: unique_title_leader_rows
unique_title_leader_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.ACTIVITY_TITLE AS activity_title,
  s.SESSION_LOCATION AS location,
  d.CREATE_DATE AS term_start_date,
  p.PERSON_NAME AS person_name
FROM iap_subject_detail d
JOIN iap_subject_person p
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_session s
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
WHERE p.PERSON_ROLE = 'Activity leader'
GROUP BY
  d.ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  s.SESSION_LOCATION,
  d.CREATE_DATE,
  p.PERSON_NAME
unique_title_leader_rows.description: From activity-with-supervisors, filter to rows where person_role exactly equals 'Activity leader', then deduplicate to one row per unique activity_title, keeping activity title, location, term_start_date, and supervisor name. Ordering by term_start_date will be applied at final output.

locations_offices.name: locations_offices
locations_offices.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS location_id,
  NULL AS person_id,
  `BUILDING_ROOM` AS room,
  `FLOOR` AS floor,
  `BUILDING_COMPONENT` AS building_key,
  `SPACE_UNIT_CODE` AS address_id
FROM `zpm_rooms_load`
WHERE `SPACE_USAGE` = 'Office'
  AND `HR_ORG_UNIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `SPACE_UNIT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
locations_offices.description: All office/location records that link a person to an office room and building (room number, floor, building key, and a foreign key to addresses).

subject_titles.name: subject_titles
subject_titles.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(sos.`SUBJECT_ID`, so.`SUBJECT_ID`, ss.`SUBJECT_ID`, se.`SUBJECT_ID`, dcc.`SUBJECT_ID`, lso.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS subject_id,
  -- Prefer authoritative short title sources in this order, falling back to any available title
  COALESCE(
    sos.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    so.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    ss.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    se.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    dcc.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    lso.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
  ) AS subject_title
FROM
  -- anchor list of subject identifiers comes from subject_summary (one row per subject)
  `subject_summary` ss
  LEFT JOIN `subject_offered_summary` sos
    ON sos.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY` = ss.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`
    AND sos.`TERM_CODE` = ss.`TERM_CODE`
    AND sos.`SUBJECT_ID` = ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
  LEFT JOIN `subject_offered` so
    ON so.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY` = ss.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`
    AND so.`TERM_CODE` = ss.`TERM_CODE`
    AND so.`SUBJECT_ID` = ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
  LEFT JOIN `subject_enrollable` se
    ON se.`TERM_CODE` = ss.`TERM_CODE`
    AND se.`SUBJECT_ID` = ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` dcc
    ON dcc.`SUBJECT_ID` = ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
  LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered` lso
    ON lso.`TERM_CODE` = ss.`TERM_CODE`
    AND lso.`SUBJECT_ID` = ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
GROUP BY
  ss.`SUBJECT_ID`
subject_titles.description: Map from subject identifier (or subject + catalog) to the subject title used for display.
counter_examples: What are the subject titles, their material titles, ISBN numbers, and total costs of new materials for each subject title?

courses_owned_by_cis.name: courses_owned_by_cis
courses_owned_by_cis.body_sql:
SELECT
  cos.`SECTION_ID`        AS course_id,
  cos.`SECTION_ID`        AS section_id,
  lr.`building_key`       AS building_key,
  bld.`BUILDING_NAME`     AS building_name
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS cos
LEFT JOIN locations_offices AS lr
  ON cos.`MEET_PLACE` = lr.`location_id`
LEFT JOIN buildings AS bld
  ON lr.`building_key` = bld.`BUILDING_KEY`
WHERE
  cos.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = 'CIS'
courses_owned_by_cis.description: Select course offering rows that are owned/managed by the Center for International Studies (CIS). This filters the course/section/course_owner relation to only CIS entries (do not aggregate).

buildings_reference.name: buildings_reference
buildings_reference.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name
FROM buildings b
buildings_reference.description: All buildings (keys and names) from the buildings/building_locations table to ensure building metadata is available for join or for including zero-count buildings if the join strategy allows.

building_cis_summary.name: building_cis_summary
building_cis_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
  IFNULL(c.cis_course_count, 0) AS cis_course_count
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    cb.building_key AS building_key,
    COUNT(*) AS cis_course_count
  FROM courses_owned_by_cis cb
  GROUP BY cb.building_key
) c ON c.building_key = b.BUILDING_KEY
building_cis_summary.description: Left-join the buildings reference to the CIS course counts to produce one row per building_key with building name and the count of CIS courses; depending on desired inclusion rules, this will either produce only buildings with counts (inner join) or include all buildings with zero where counts are missing (left join).

term_dimensions_sel.name: term_dimensions_sel
term_dimensions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  at.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS term_description
FROM academic_terms_all AS at
GROUP BY at.TERM_CODE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION
term_dimensions_sel.description: Select canonical term-level attributes (term code and term description) for each term that may be referenced by sessions. One row per term.
counter_examples: For each term code, list the term description, attribute desciption, department name, school name, and the number of subjects in the area of humanities, arts and social sciences.

iap_session_term_join.name: iap_session_term_join
iap_session_term_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,
  d.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  f.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION AS term_description,
  d.FEE AS fee,
  d.ATTENDANCE AS enrollment
FROM iap_subject_session AS s
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS d
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN frc_fiscal_periods AS f
  ON d.TERM_CODE = f.TIME_MONTH_KEY
iap_session_term_join.description: Join IAP sessions to term dimension to attach canonical term description to each IAP session row. Preserve one row per session with its term fields.

iap_term_aggregates.name: iap_term_aggregates
iap_term_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  f.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION AS term_description,
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS iap_session_count,
  SUM(d.FEE) AS total_fee_collected,
  MIN(d.MAX_ENROLLMENT) AS min_enrollment,
  MAX(d.MAX_ENROLLMENT) AS max_enrollment
FROM iap_subject_detail d
JOIN frc_fiscal_periods f
  ON f.TIME_MONTH_KEY = d.TERM_CODE
WHERE d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  d.TERM_CODE,
  f.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) > 0
iap_term_aggregates.description: Aggregate IAP sessions per term to compute counts and enrollment/fee aggregates: count of IAP sessions, sum of fees collected, min enrollment, and max enrollment. Do not include terms with zero IAP sessions (only terms with at least one aggregated session will appear).

iap_session_times_norm.name: iap_session_times_norm
iap_session_times_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS subject_id,
  ss.SESSION_LOCATION AS building,
  d.FEE AS fee,
  -- parse start and end times stored as strings in format like 'hhmmap' or 'hmmam' etc (format '%h%i%p')
  -- convert to TIME then to minutes since midnight
  TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_START_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60 AS start_minutes,
  TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_END_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60 AS end_minutes,
  -- compute duration in minutes, handling overnight spans: if end_minutes < start_minutes, add 24*60
  (
    (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_END_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60)
    - (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_START_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60)
    + CASE
        WHEN (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_END_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60) < (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(ss.SESSION_START_TIME, '%h%i%p'))/60)
        THEN 24*60
        ELSE 0
      END
  ) AS duration_minutes
FROM iap_subject_session s
JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session ss
  ON ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
iap_session_times_norm.description: Normalize and parse SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME strings (format '%h%i%p') into canonical time/datetime or minute-of-day values and compute session duration (end - start) in minutes taking into account possible overnight spans if needed.

subject_fee_per_session.name: subject_fee_per_session
subject_fee_per_session.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through source keys as required
  si.`SESSION_NUMBER` AS session_id,
  si.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,
  si.`MEET_PLACE` AS building,
  sd.`FEE` AS fee,
  -- compute duration in minutes from meet start/end times when present; keep NULL if not derivable
  CASE
    WHEN si.`MEET_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
     AND si.`MEET_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
     AND si.`MEET_START_TIME` <> ''
     AND si.`MEET_END_TIME` <> ''
    THEN
      -- parse as time; supports formats like 'HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS'
      TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(si.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%H:%i:%s'))/60
      - TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(si.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%H:%i:%s'))/60
  END AS duration_minutes
FROM
  `subject_iap_schedule` si
  -- join to subject detail to get the stored FEE and ensure mapping by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail` sd
    ON sd.`TERM_CODE` = si.`TERM_CODE`
    AND sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = si.`SESSION_NUMBER`
    -- Also ensure subject id mapping: SUBJECT_ID corresponds to IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY or subject key pattern.
    -- Because exact subject id column resides in subject_iap_schedule (SUBJECT_ID) and fee resides in iap_subject_detail,
    -- we join on TERM_CODE and allow session-number linkage; if additional keys are needed they should be supplied externally.
    -- Do not re-derive FEE; use sd.FEE column as requested.
WHERE
  -- lift question-specific literals out: only filter to rows that have a subject id and a session number (session granularity)
  si.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND si.`SESSION_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL
subject_fee_per_session.description: Ensure one row per subject/session carrying the fee to be summed per building. If multiple session rows can map to same subject occurrence, keep distinct subject-session pairs with their fee and duration.

iap_virtual_rows_sel.name: iap_virtual_rows_sel
iap_virtual_rows_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- row identifier: use the session key if available, else fall back to subject category key plus session sequence to preserve uniqueness
  COALESCE(s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`, CONCAT(d.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`, '-', IFNULL(s.`SESSION_SEQUENCE`, '0'))) AS row_id,

  -- subject id comes from detail table TERM_CODE/subject id mapping: the schema only has SUBJECT_ID in subject_iap_schedule,
  -- so join that table to get SUBJECT_ID. Keep the exact column name as required.
  sch.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,

  -- fee comes from iap_subject_detail table (do NOT re-derive)
  d.`FEE` AS fee,

  -- raw session type/modality: SESSION_LOCATION in iap_subject_session appears to indicate modality/type per schema (it is key)
  s.`SESSION_LOCATION` AS session_type_raw,

  -- raw term/period: TERM_CODE in iap_subject_detail
  d.`TERM_CODE` AS term_period_raw,

  -- raw start/end times: use schedule MEET_START_TIME / MEET_END_TIME if available, else fall back to session start/end time columns
  COALESCE(sch.`MEET_START_TIME`, s.`SESSION_START_TIME`) AS session_start_time_raw,
  COALESCE(sch.`MEET_END_TIME`, s.`SESSION_END_TIME`) AS session_end_time_raw

FROM iap_subject_detail d
  -- left join sessions so we preserve subject-level rows even if no session row exists
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session s
    ON d.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = s.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
  -- left join schedule to get SUBJECT_ID and meeting times; join condition based on term and subject identifiers:
  -- lift question-specific literals out: do not filter here by term or modality; but we must filter to "virtual" modality and "IAP" term (case-insensitive)
  LEFT JOIN subject_iap_schedule sch
    ON sch.`TERM_CODE` = d.`TERM_CODE`
       AND sch.`SUBJECT_ID` = d.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`
       AND (sch.`SESSION_NUMBER` = s.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` OR (s.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` IS NULL AND sch.`SESSION_NUMBER` IS NULL))

WHERE
  -- filter to modalities/types that indicate virtual (case-insensitive) using SESSION_LOCATION (session_type_raw) and schedule.MEET_PLACE as fallbacks;
  -- consider both SESSION_LOCATION and MEET_PLACE for modality. Use LOWER(...) LIKE '%virtual%' OR '%zoom%' OR '%online%' as common virtual indicators.
  (
    (s.`SESSION_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(s.`SESSION_LOCATION`) LIKE '%virtual%')
    OR (s.`SESSION_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(s.`SESSION_LOCATION`) LIKE '%zoom%')
    OR (s.`SESSION_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(s.`SESSION_LOCATION`) LIKE '%online%')
    OR (sch.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(sch.`MEET_PLACE`) LIKE '%virtual%')
    OR (sch.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(sch.`MEET_PLACE`) LIKE '%zoom%')
    OR (sch.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(sch.`MEET_PLACE`) LIKE '%online%')
  )

  -- filter to terms/periods that indicate IAP (case-insensitive) using TERM_CODE
  AND d.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(d.`TERM_CODE`) LIKE '%iap%'
iap_virtual_rows_sel.description: Select rows that represent sessions and filter to those whose modality/type indicates virtual (case-insensitive) and whose term/period indicates IAP (case-insensitive). Keep rows even if start/end times are null or invalid; those will be excluded later only for duration calculations.

iap_virtual_normalized_times.name: iap_virtual_normalized_times
iap_virtual_normalized_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- row identifier: use the session key to represent a distinct row_id (carried through)
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS row_id,

  -- subject_id: from subject detail table (must join to get this exact column)
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS subject_id,

  -- fee: from subject detail table (exact stored column)
  d.FEE AS fee,

  -- session_type: canonicalized modality/period. Use SESSION_DESCRIPTION as source for session_type
  -- lowercase canonicalization
  LOWER(s.SESSION_DESCRIPTION) AS session_type,

  -- term_period: canonicalized term code / period from subject detail TERM_CODE
  LOWER(d.TERM_CODE) AS term_period,

  -- start_minutes: parse SESSION_START_TIME using format '%h%i%p' into TIME then minutes since midnight.
  -- If parsing fails, result will be NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN s.SESSION_START_TIME IS NULL OR s.SESSION_START_TIME = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- STR_TO_DATE returns NULL on parse failure
      (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%h%i%p')) DIV 60)
  END AS start_minutes,

  -- end_minutes: similarly for SESSION_END_TIME
  CASE
    WHEN s.SESSION_END_TIME IS NULL OR s.SESSION_END_TIME = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (TIME_TO_SEC(STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%h%i%p')) DIV 60)
  END AS end_minutes,

  -- start_valid: boolean flag (1/0) indicating parsed start is valid (non-null after parsing)
  CASE
    WHEN s.SESSION_START_TIME IS NULL OR s.SESSION_START_TIME = '' THEN 0
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%h%i%p') IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS start_valid,

  -- end_valid: boolean flag for end time
  CASE
    WHEN s.SESSION_END_TIME IS NULL OR s.SESSION_END_TIME = '' THEN 0
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%h%i%p') IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS end_valid

FROM iap_subject_session AS s
-- join to subject detail to pull stored subject-level columns such as FEE and TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS d
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
iap_virtual_normalized_times.description: Normalize and canonicalize SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME strings into a consistent parsed-time representation (e.g. minutes-since-midnight or a time type) using the '%h%i%p' format; mark rows with invalid or NULL parsed times. Also canonicalize modality and period strings to lowercase for consistent matching.

component_room_aggregates.name: component_room_aggregates
component_room_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.BUILDING_COMPONENT AS component_id,
  sd.BUILDING_COMPONENT AS component_name,
  sd.BUILDING_KEY AS building_id,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
  SUM(sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS total_room_sqft,
  SUM(sd.ROOM_COUNTER) AS room_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sd.ROOM_NUMBER) AS distinct_floor_count
FROM space_detail sd
LEFT JOIN fac_building b
  ON sd.BUILDING_KEY = b.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  sd.BUILDING_COMPONENT,
  sd.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME
component_room_aggregates.description: Per building component, aggregate room-level measures: sum of room square footage, count of rooms, and count of distinct floors that those rooms occupy. Keeps one row per component (and includes building identifiers/names so component → building is preserved).

enrollment_by_department.name: enrollment_by_department
enrollment_by_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(su.DEPARTMENT_CODE, so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE) AS department_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(su.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)),
           SUM(COALESCE(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)),
           SUM(COALESCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)),
           0) AS total_enrolled_students
FROM subject_summary su
LEFT JOIN subject_offered_summary sos ON sos.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY = su.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so ON so.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY = su.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY
GROUP BY COALESCE(su.DEPARTMENT_CODE, so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE)
enrollment_by_department.description: Total enrolled students per department aggregated from enrollment/student records. Treat NULL enrollments as zero or exclude per DB semantics; produce one row per department with summed enrollment.

term_code_normalized.name: term_code_normalized
term_code_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  -- extract last 2 characters as TT suffix; keep as-is (do not alter source TERM_CODE)
  RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE, 2) AS term_tt_suffix,
  -- map TT suffix to canonical description
  CASE
    WHEN RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE, 2) IN ('FA','F1','F2','F3') THEN 'Fall'
    WHEN RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE, 2) IN ('SP','S1','S2') THEN 'Spring'
    WHEN RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE, 2) IN ('SU','SU','S3') THEN 'Summer'
    WHEN RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE, 2) IN ('IP','IA','AP') OR RIGHT(at.TERM_CODE,2) = 'I0' THEN 'IAP'
    ELSE at.TERM_DESCRIPTION
  END AS term_description,
  -- normalize IS_CURRENT_TERM flag to 'Y' or 'N'; treat common truthy values as 'Y'
  CASE
    WHEN at.IS_CURRENT_TERM IN ('Y','y','YES','Yes','true','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_current_term
FROM academic_terms at
term_code_normalized.description: Normalize/parse the term code to produce the two-character TT suffix and map it to a canonical TERM_DESCRIPTION value ('Fall','IAP','Spring','Summer'); also normalize the IS_CURRENT_TERM flag to 'Y' or 'N'.

normalized_columns.name: normalized_columns
normalized_columns.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- row identifier: prefer a stored primary/key column from available tables.
  -- Several source tables have explicit KEY columns; choose TIP_MATERIAL_KEY when present,
  -- otherwise fall back to other table keys by LEFT JOINs so row_id is always from a real stored column.
  COALESCE(t.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, r.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY, s.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, c.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY, m.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY, tm.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY) AS row_id,

  -- AUTHOR cleaned: preserve exactly as stored in tip_material.AUTHOR, but trim surrounding whitespace;
  -- keep NULLs if AUTHOR is NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(t.AUTHOR), '') AS author_clean,

  -- SCHOOL cleaned: the schema has OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME on tip_subject_offered; keep exact stored value, trimmed.
  NULLIF(TRIM(s.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME), '') AS school_clean,

  -- MATERIAL STATUS cleaned: prefer library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS, trimmed, else tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
  NULLIF(TRIM(m.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS), '') AS material_status_clean,

  -- COURSE TYPE cleaned: there is no explicit "course_type" column in these tables; however
  -- LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR.COURSE_NAME exists and represents course identification/type — preserve stored value trimmed.
  NULLIF(TRIM(c.COURSE_NAME), '') AS course_type_clean

FROM tip_material t
  -- left join to library_reserve_catalog to allow using its key as row_id when tip_material is absent in a broader UNION scenario;
  -- joins are written but not enforced to avoid losing rows from tip_material.
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog r
    ON r.CATALOG_ISBN = t.ISBN
  -- join to tip_subject_offered to get OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME (school_clean) when available by matching subject/title heuristics:
  LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered s
    ON s.SUBJECT_TITLE = t.TITLE
  -- left join to library_course_instructor to get course_name for course_type_clean when available by matching course title/name:
  LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor c
    ON c.COURSE_NAME = t.TITLE
  -- left join to library_material_status to get stored material status when it can be related by code/name to tip_material (no direct FK in schema),
  -- attempt to match on exact text equality with TIP_MATERIAL.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE (best-effort). This preserves source column usage.
  LEFT JOIN library_material_status m
    ON m.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS = t.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE
  -- left join to tip_material_status in case tip_material_status entries are needed for completeness (not used above but carried for row_id fallback)
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tm
    ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS = t.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE
normalized_columns.description: Project and canonicalize the relevant columns (ensure AUTHOR and SCHOOL kept exactly as stored, preserve NULLs, trim or cast types if needed) producing cleaned fields for grouping.

tip_subjects_norm.name: tip_subjects_norm
tip_subjects_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical term code: use tip_subject_offered.TERM_CODE as-is (lifted from source)
  t.TERM_CODE                                                     AS term_code,

  -- term_description: canonicalize by mapping TERM_CODE to a human-friendly description.
  -- We derive description from TERM_CODE format like YYYYMM or YYYYQ (common patterns).
  -- Keep original when pattern not matched.
  CASE
    WHEN t.TERM_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}0[1-9]$' THEN CONCAT(SUBSTR(t.TERM_CODE,1,4), '-Spring')   -- e.g. 202201 -> 2022-Spring
    WHEN t.TERM_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}0[2-9]$' THEN CONCAT(SUBSTR(t.TERM_CODE,1,4), '-Fall')     -- fallback for other codes
    WHEN t.TERM_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}[0-9]{2}$' THEN CONCAT(SUBSTR(t.TERM_CODE,1,4), '-Term ', CAST(SUBSTR(t.TERM_CODE,5,2) AS UNSIGNED))
    ELSE t.TERM_CODE
  END                                                              AS term_description,

  -- term_current_flag: normalized boolean indicator based on TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE relative to current date.
  -- If WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE is present and within the last 180 days mark as 1, else 0. NULLs -> 0.
  CASE
    WHEN t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
         AND STR_TO_DATE(t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 180 DAY) THEN 1
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y/%m/%d') IS NOT NULL
         AND STR_TO_DATE(t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y/%m/%d') >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 180 DAY) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END                                                              AS term_current_flag,

  -- subject_id: carry through the exact column from tip_subject_offered
  t.SUBJECT_ID                                                     AS subject_id,

  -- school_id: use OFFER_DEPT_CODE as the school identifier (carry exact column)
  t.OFFER_DEPT_CODE                                                AS school_id,

  -- materials_clean: normalized/trimmed concatenation of associated material identifiers/titles for the subject record.
  -- We gather distinct material titles/ISBNs from tip_detail -> tip_material, trim whitespace, and produce a comma list.
  -- Keep original exact columns from tip_material (ISBN and TITLE) present in source tables.
  NULLIF(
    TRIM(
      GROUP_CONCAT(
        DISTINCT CONCAT(
          COALESCE(TRIM(tm.ISBN), ''),
          CASE WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(tm.ISBN,'')) <> '' AND TRIM(COALESCE(tm.TITLE,'')) <> '' THEN ' :: ' ELSE '' END,
          COALESCE(TRIM(tm.TITLE), '')
        ) ORDER BY tm.ISBN, tm.TITLE SEPARATOR ', '
      )
    ), ''
  )                                                                 AS materials_clean,

  -- enrolled_count_clean: normalized numeric enrolled count from tip_subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS.
  -- Preserve numeric value; if NULL or non-positive, produce NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS < 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
  END                                                              AS enrolled_count_clean,

  -- carry keys to preserve joinability (grain: one row per subject record)
  t.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY                                         AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

FROM tip_subject_offered t

-- join to tip_detail to find materials linked to this subject record (left join to keep subjects with no materials)
LEFT JOIN tip_detail d
  ON d.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = t.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

-- join to tip_material to pull canonical material fields (ISBN, TITLE). Use LEFT JOIN so missing materials don't drop the subject.
LEFT JOIN tip_material tm
  ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = d.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY

GROUP BY
  t.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  t.TERM_CODE,
  t.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  t.SUBJECT_ID,
  t.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
tip_subjects_norm.description: Normalize/clean fields on each TIP subject record: canonicalize term code and description, normalize the term current indicator to a boolean flag, trim/standardize materials values, and ensure enrolled_count is numeric (NULLs handled).

floor_assignable_area.name: floor_assignable_area
floor_assignable_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- floor_id: use the canonical floor key from fac_floor when available,
  -- otherwise fall back to space_floor.floor_key to ensure one row per floor.
  COALESCE(f.`FLOOR_KEY`, sf.`FLOOR_KEY`) AS floor_id,

  -- assignable_floor_area: prefer the stored canonical floor assignable area from fac_floor.
  -- If that's NULL, fall back to the sum of room AREA from fac_rooms for that floor (to cover cases
  -- where the fac_floor stored value is missing). The fallback is computed by a correlated aggregate
  -- (left join to a derived totals table) so we still expose the stored source where present.
  COALESCE(f.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`, fr_tot.floor_assignable_sum) AS assignable_floor_area

FROM
  -- primary source for canonical floor-level stored values
  `fac_floor` f

  -- space_floor included to ensure floors that exist in space_floor but not in fac_floor
  -- are still represented (LEFT JOIN from fac_floor keeps canonical rows; UNION-like coverage
  -- for missing fac_floor rows will be handled by a UNION in a separate SELECT below).
  LEFT JOIN `space_floor` sf
    ON f.`FLOOR_KEY` = sf.`FLOOR_KEY`

  -- derived table with per-floor sums of room AREA from fac_rooms
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      fr.`FLOOR_KEY` AS floor_key,
      SUM(fr.`AREA`) AS floor_assignable_sum
    FROM `fac_rooms` fr
    GROUP BY fr.`FLOOR_KEY`
  ) fr_tot
    ON fr_tot.floor_key = f.`FLOOR_KEY`

UNION ALL

-- Include floors that exist in space_floor but do not have a fac_floor row.
-- For those, use space_floor.FLOOR_KEY as floor_id and get assignable area from fac_rooms sums.
SELECT
  sf.`FLOOR_KEY` AS floor_id,
  COALESCE(fr_tot2.floor_assignable_sum, NULL) AS assignable_floor_area
FROM `space_floor` sf
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    fr.`FLOOR_KEY` AS floor_key,
    SUM(fr.`AREA`) AS floor_assignable_sum
  FROM `fac_rooms` fr
  GROUP BY fr.`FLOOR_KEY`
) fr_tot2
  ON fr_tot2.floor_key = sf.`FLOOR_KEY`
WHERE sf.`FLOOR_KEY` NOT IN (SELECT `FLOOR_KEY` FROM `fac_floor`)
floor_assignable_area.description: Assignable area for each floor (sum of assignable room areas or canonical floor assignable area), one row per floor. This computes the total assignable area for the floor that will be used to compute room-area-as-percent-of-floor.

instructors_norm.name: instructors_norm
instructors_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical instructor identifier: prefer MIT_ID from tables that have it, otherwise fall back to available keys/names
  COALESCE(NULLIF(hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(se_person.MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(opa_person_current.MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(drupal_course_catalog.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(employee_directory.MIT_ID, ''),
           NULLIF(warehouse_users.MIT_ID, ''),
           -- if no MIT_ID available, use a stable person key where present
           NULLIF(iap_subject_person.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY, ''),
           NULLIF(library_course_instructor.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, ''),
           -- final fallback: full name concatenations (kept as stored FULL_NAME columns where available)
           NULLIF(iap_subject_person.PERSON_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(opa_person_current.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(drupal_employee_directory.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(employee_directory.FULL_NAME, '')
          ) AS instructor_id,

  -- canonical display name: prefer stored full-name columns in sources; preserve exact stored value (no reconstruction)
  COALESCE(NULLIF(hr_faculty_roster.FIRST_NAME, '') /* use FIRST_NAME if that's the only stored name available */,
           NULLIF(hr_faculty_roster.LAST_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(iap_subject_person.PERSON_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(library_course_instructor.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(se_person.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(opa_person_current.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(drupal_employee_directory.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(employee_directory.FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(warehouse_users.FIRST_NAME, ''),
           NULLIF(warehouse_users.LAST_NAME, '')
          ) AS instructor_name

FROM hr_faculty_roster
  -- left join many possible identity sources so we can coalesce across them without filtering out rows
  LEFT JOIN se_person
    ON se_person.MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN opa_person_current
    ON opa_person_current.MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog
    ON drupal_course_catalog.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail
    ON moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory
    ON employee_directory.MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN warehouse_users
    ON warehouse_users.MIT_ID = hr_faculty_roster.MIT_ID

  -- also include rows coming from sources that may not have MIT_IDs by left-joining them via loose name matches
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_person
    ON iap_subject_person.PERSON_NAME = CONCAT(COALESCE(hr_faculty_roster.FIRST_NAME, ''), COALESCE(' ', ''), COALESCE(hr_faculty_roster.LAST_NAME, ''))
  LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor
    ON library_course_instructor.INSTRUCTOR_NAME = iap_subject_person.PERSON_NAME
  LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory
    ON drupal_employee_directory.FULL_NAME = iap_subject_person.PERSON_NAME

-- Deduplicate: group by the chosen instructor_id to produce one row per instructor_id (grain)
GROUP BY instructor_id, instructor_name
instructors_norm.description: Normalize/clean instructor identity information producing one row per instructor with a canonical display name or identifier to use in results.

normalized_instructor_info.name: normalized_instructor_info
normalized_instructor_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical instructor id: prefer MIT_ID from employee_directory, fall back to MIT_ID from warehouse_users,
  -- finally use INSTRUCTOR_NAME from library_course_instructor (trimmed) as last resort
  NULLIF(TRIM(ed.MIT_ID), '') AS instructor_id,
  -- canonical instructor name: prefer FULL_NAME from employee_directory, then FULL_NAME from drupal_employee_directory,
  -- finally INSTRUCTOR_NAME from library_course_instructor (trimmed)
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(TRIM(ed.FULL_NAME), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(ded.FULL_NAME), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME), '')
  ) AS instructor_name,
  -- canonical instructor email: prefer EMAIL_ADDRESS from employee_directory, then warehouse_users.EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  -- then drupal_employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS; blank strings normalized to NULL
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(TRIM(ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(wu.EMAIL_ADDRESS), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(ded.EMAIL_ADDRESS), '')
  ) AS instructor_email
FROM
  -- start from library_course_instructor fall-term records (this view is meant for fall-term canonicalization);
  -- keep all distinct instructors present there so grain is one row per instructor identifier (MIT_ID when available)
  (SELECT DISTINCT INSTRUCTOR_NAME, UNIT_CODE, UNIT, WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE FROM library_course_instructor) AS lci
  -- left join to employee_directory on matching name variants first by FULL_NAME, then by LAST/FIRST if available.
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory AS ed
    ON (
         -- prefer exact match on full name (case-sensitive per schema rules); also allow match if ed.FULL_NAME equals lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
         (ed.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL AND ed.FULL_NAME = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME)
       )
  -- fallback join to warehouse_users to bring emails/MIT_ID if employee_directory not present
  LEFT JOIN warehouse_users AS wu
    ON (
         -- try to match by name fields when available
         ( (wu.FIRST_NAME IS NOT NULL AND wu.LAST_NAME IS NOT NULL)
           AND CONCAT(TRIM(wu.FIRST_NAME), ' ', TRIM(wu.LAST_NAME)) = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
         )
         OR (wu.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND wu.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID)
       )
  -- drupal employee directory may have additional email/name info; left join by name
  LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS ded
    ON (ded.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL AND ded.FULL_NAME = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME)
WHERE
  -- restrict to fall-term related rows by heuristics on UNIT/UNIT_CODE being non-null OR instructor name present;
  -- lift literals out of view in calling queries; here we simply ensure instructor name exists
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME IS NOT NULL
normalized_instructor_info.description: Canonicalize instructor identifiers, names, and emails (trim/NULL-handling) from the fall-term records so each instructor is represented consistently for joins and grouping.

building_unit_aggregates.name: building_unit_aggregates
building_unit_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS total_gross_sq_ft,
  SUM(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS total_assignable_sq_ft,
  COUNT(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS assignable_unit_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT z.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID ORDER BY z.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID SEPARATOR ',') AS hr_department_names
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN zpm_rooms_load AS z
  ON z.BUILDING_COMPONENT = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY
building_unit_aggregates.description: Aggregate normalized rows by building_key to compute sums and counts per building: sum of gross_sq_ft_num, sum of assignable_sq_ft_num, and count of rows used to compute average assignable sqft. Also collect distinct HR department_name values per building (one row per building, but department list kept as a multivalue/array).

FROM `moira_list_detail`

global_member_count_extrema.name: global_member_count_extrema
global_member_count_extrema.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(MAX_counts.member_count AS SIGNED) AS member_count,
  MAX_counts.extrema_type AS extrema_type
FROM (
  SELECT
    MAX(CAST(mld.COUNTER AS SIGNED)) AS member_count,
    'MAX' AS extrema_type
  FROM moira_list_detail mld
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    MIN(CAST(mld.COUNTER AS SIGNED)) AS member_count,
    'MIN' AS extrema_type
  FROM moira_list_detail mld
) AS MAX_counts
global_member_count_extrema.description: Compute the global maximum and minimum member_count values across all mailing lists (one row for each of the two extrema values). This identifies the member_count thresholds for selecting lists tied at max or min.

student_cohort_counts.name: student_cohort_counts
student_cohort_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) AS student_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS department_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sd.SCHOOL_CODE) AS school_count
FROM moira_list_detail AS m
LEFT JOIN student_department AS sd
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE -- lifted literal: replace at combine-time if different join key needed
student_cohort_counts.description: Aggregate the joined student-on-list rows to compute the distinct student count and distinct counts of SIS departments and SIS schools among that cohort. (Final filters such as moira_list_name = 'candle-duo-users' are applied at combine time.)

moira_list_members_student_cohort.name: moira_list_members_student_cohort
moira_list_members_student_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS moira_list_name,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS member_id,
  s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS sis_admin_department_name,
  CASE
    WHEN d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER LIKE '%@mit.edu' OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_student_flag
FROM moira_list m
JOIN moira_list_detail d
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department s
  ON s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
WHERE m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y'
  AND (d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER LIKE '%@mit.edu')
moira_list_members_student_cohort.description: Select the cohort of members for a given moira list restricted to rows that represent students in the SIS. Keep member identifiers and the SIS department name as provided in the source.

student_department_normalized.name: student_department_normalized
student_department_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through requested ids exactly as-named from source tables
  s.MIT_ID                                AS person_id,
  CONCAT('MEM-', COALESCE(s.MIT_ID, ''))  AS membership_id,
  -- Normalize department: prefer authoritative HR unit mappings when available;
  -- trim whitespace, null-to-empty, collapse multiple internal spaces, and upper-case for canonical comparison.
  NULLIF(
    TRIM(
      UPPER(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
          COALESCE(o.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, ou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, s.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE, s.ADMIN_ORG_UNIT_TITLE, s.DIRECTORY_ORG_UNIT_TITLE, '')
        , '\\s+', ' ')
      )
    )
  , '') AS department
FROM hr_faculty_roster s
LEFT JOIN hr_org_unit_new o
  ON s.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = o.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE
LEFT JOIN hr_org_unit ou
  ON s.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = ou.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE
student_department_normalized.description: Normalize and canonicalize the department representation for each student-member (clean nulls, trim/standardize department text or map department codes to names) so department values are comparable across students.

attribute_subject_aggregates.name: attribute_subject_aggregates
attribute_subject_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  ca.HASS_ATTRIBUTE                                    AS attribute_key,
  ca.HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC                               AS attribute_name,
  ha.DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN                          AS attribute_description,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ca.SUBJECT_ID)                       AS num_unique_subjects,
  AVG(COALESCE(ca.TOTAL_UNITS, 0))                    AS avg_units_across_subjects,
  SUM(COALESCE(ca.TOTAL_UNITS, 0) * 0) + SUM(0)       AS total_enrollment_across_subjects,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ca.DEPARTMENT_CODE)                  AS num_degree_granting_departments
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS ca
LEFT JOIN
  cis_hass_attribute AS ha
    ON ca.HASS_ATTRIBUTE = ha.HASS_ATTRIBUTE
GROUP BY
  ca.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  ca.HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC,
  ha.DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN
attribute_subject_aggregates.description: Aggregate across subjects that hold the same HASS attribute: count distinct subjects, average of subject-level units (average of subject_units_avg), sum of subject total enrollments, count of distinct departments that are degree-granting among departments associated with those subjects. Also carry attribute name and description forward.

global_total.name: global_total
global_total.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(SUM(fr.AREA), 0) AS global_total_area,
  COALESCE(COUNT(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY), 0) AS global_room_count
FROM fac_rooms fr
global_total.description: Compute overall totals across all buildings: sum of all room areas and total room count. This supplies the grand total row and denominators for building-level percentage computations that must be relative to the total area across all buildings.

metrics_per_fin_aid_and_acad_year.name: metrics_per_fin_aid_and_acad_year
metrics_per_fin_aid_and_acad_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  tafy.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR                              AS financial_aid_year,
  tafy.ACADEMIC_YEAR                                   AS academic_year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tm.FISCAL_PERIOD)                     AS num_fiscal_periods,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tq.FY_QUARTER_CODE)                   AS num_quarters,
  MIN(NULLIF(atp.TERM_START_DATE, ''))                 AS start_term_date,
  MAX(NULLIF(atp.TERM_END_DATE, ''))                   AS end_term_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(atp.TERM_PARAMETER, ''))       AS num_distinct_department_level_term_parameters
FROM
  -- Use time_month as the driver for fiscal periods and financial aid year / academic year
  time_month tm
  -- join to time_quarter to get quarter identifiers for the same fiscal year or quarter range
  LEFT JOIN time_quarter tq
    ON tq.FISCAL_YEAR = tm.FISCAL_YEAR
  -- join to academic_term_parameter to pick up term-level parameters (department-level term parameters)
  LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter atp
    ON atp.TERM_CODE = tm.ACADEMIC_TERM
  -- Also include academic_terms/all tables if they carry financial_aid_year & academic_year consistently.
  -- Use a derived table (tafy) that selects the pair (financial_aid_year, academic_year) from the available tables.
  -- We prefer time_month as source of both FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR and ACADEMIC_YEAR when present.
  JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      NULLIF(FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR, '') AS FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
      NULLIF(ACADEMIC_YEAR, '') AS ACADEMIC_YEAR
    FROM time_month
  ) tafy
    ON tafy.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR = NULLIF(tm.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR, '')
   AND tafy.ACADEMIC_YEAR = NULLIF(tm.ACADEMIC_YEAR, '')
GROUP BY
  tafy.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  tafy.ACADEMIC_YEAR
metrics_per_fin_aid_and_acad_year.description: Aggregate metrics per (financial_aid_year, academic_year): count of distinct fiscal_period_id, count of distinct quarter_id, earliest (min) start_term_date (ignoring nulls), latest (max) end_term_date (ignoring nulls), and count of distinct non-null department_level_term_parameter. This final step combines the prepared inputs to produce one row per financial aid year + academic year.

ownership_summary_prep.name: ownership_summary_prep
ownership_summary_prep.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable building identifier from a base table
  COALESCE(f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, b.BUILDING_KEY, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) AS building_id,

  -- building number from base tables (preserve exact stored columns)
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_NUMBER, fb.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS building_number,

  -- full name: prefer fac_building.BUILDING_NAME, then buildings.BUILDING_NAME, then fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NAME, b.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME) AS full_name,

  -- address_text: prefer fac_building_address fields if present, else fclt_building_address CITY/STATE/POSTAL_CODE, else buildings STREET/MAILING
  TRIM(
    CONCAT(
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER, cba.STREET_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS, ''),
      CASE WHEN COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER, cba.STREET_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME, cba.STREET_NAME) IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME, cba.STREET_NAME, ''),
      CASE WHEN (COALESCE(fba.CITY, cba.CITY, b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) IS NOT NULL) THEN CONCAT(', ', COALESCE(fba.CITY, cba.CITY, b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS)) ELSE '' END,
      CASE WHEN COALESCE(fba.STATE, cba.STATE) IS NOT NULL THEN CONCAT(', ', COALESCE(fba.STATE, cba.STATE)) ELSE '' END,
      CASE WHEN COALESCE(fba.POSTAL_CODE, cba.POSTAL_CODE) IS NOT NULL THEN CONCAT(' ', COALESCE(fba.POSTAL_CODE, cba.POSTAL_CODE)) ELSE '' END
    )
  ) AS address_text,

  -- building type taken from available base tables (do not substitute)
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_TYPE, fb.BUILDING_TYPE) AS building_type,

  -- occupancy_date: use DATE_OCCUPIED from fac_building if available, else DATE_OCCUPIED from fclt_building
  COALESCE(f.DATE_OCCUPIED, fb.DATE_OCCUPIED) AS occupancy_date,

  -- ownership_type: take the exact stored column from fac_building or fclt_building (do not derive)
  COALESCE(f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE, fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE) AS ownership_type,

  -- site from base tables
  COALESCE(f.SITE, fb.SITE) AS site,

  -- is_owned_flag: normalized flag (1/0) set when ownership_type (exact stored column) equals 'OWNED' (case-insensitive)
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE, fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE)) = 'OWNED' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_owned_flag,

  -- is_leased_flag: normalized flag (1/0) set when ownership_type equals 'LEASED' (case-insensitive)
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE, fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE)) = 'LEASED' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_leased_flag

FROM fac_building f
  -- left join fac_building_address to get authoritative address pieces when available
  LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fba
    ON f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fba.BUILDING_KEY

  -- join to buildings table to ensure availability of buildings.* columns if present
  LEFT JOIN buildings b
    ON b.BUILDING_KEY = COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_KEY, NULL)
    -- Note: we don't assume BUILDING_KEY = BUILDING_NUMBER universally; join is permissive via COALESCE fallback

  -- left join fclt_building and its address as alternate sources (do not overwrite stored columns)
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building fb
    ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = COALESCE(f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY)

  LEFT JOIN fclt_building_address cba
    ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = cba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
ownership_summary_prep.description: Compute per-building row flags for ownership categories among the joined building rows so they can be counted later (one row per building-row from join). Do not collapse buildings here; produce a row per building-row with normalized ownership label values (e.g., 'OWNED' or 'LEASED' or other).

ownership_usage_rollups.name: ownership_usage_rollups
ownership_usage_rollups.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- ownership_type_group: sourced from fac_building.OWNERSHIP_TYPE
  fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE AS ownership_type_group,

  -- usage_type_group: sourced from fac_building.BUILDING_USE
  fb.BUILDING_USE AS usage_type_group,

  -- number_of_buildings: count distinct BUILDING_NUMBER from fac_building (building identifier present on that table)
  COUNT(DISTINCT fb.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS number_of_buildings,

  -- gross_square_footage_total: sum of BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE from buildings table joined by BUILDING_NUMBER/BUILDING_KEY relationship
  SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS gross_square_footage_total,

  -- number_of_rooms_total: sum of NUM_OF_ROOMS from fac_building (fac_building.NUM_OF_ROOMS is the stored room count per building)
  SUM(fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS number_of_rooms_total,

  -- number_of_associated_organizations_total: count distinct ORGANIZATION_KEY from fac_rooms for buildings in the group
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS number_of_associated_organizations_total,

  -- rollup_level: 0 = detail (both ownership and usage present), 1 = subtotal per ownership_type (usage blank), 2 = grand total (both blank)
  0 AS rollup_level

FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY OR fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY OR fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
-- The join above attempts to associate rooms to buildings using possible keys present in the schema:
-- fr.BUILDING_KEY may match buildings.BUILDING_KEY, fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, or fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER depending on source data linkage.

GROUP BY
  fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE,
  fb.BUILDING_USE

UNION ALL

-- Subtotal rows per ownership_type: usage blank, aggregate across usage groups for that ownership
SELECT
  fb_sub.OWNERSHIP_TYPE AS ownership_type_group,
  NULL AS usage_type_group,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fb_sub.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS number_of_buildings,
  SUM(b_sub.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS gross_square_footage_total,
  SUM(fb_sub.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS number_of_rooms_total,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr_sub.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS number_of_associated_organizations_total,
  1 AS rollup_level
FROM fac_building fb_sub
LEFT JOIN buildings b_sub
  ON b_sub.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb_sub.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr_sub
  ON fr_sub.BUILDING_KEY = b_sub.BUILDING_KEY OR fr_sub.BUILDING_KEY = fb_sub.FAC_BUILDING_KEY OR fr_sub.BUILDING_KEY = fb_sub.BUILDING_NUMBER
GROUP BY
  fb_sub.OWNERSHIP_TYPE

UNION ALL

-- Grand total row across all ownership types: both ownership and usage blank
SELECT
  NULL AS ownership_type_group,
  NULL AS usage_type_group,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fb_all.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS number_of_buildings,
  SUM(b_all.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS gross_square_footage_total,
  SUM(fb_all.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS number_of_rooms_total,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr_all.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS number_of_associated_organizations_total,
  2 AS rollup_level
FROM fac_building fb_all
LEFT JOIN buildings b_all
  ON b_all.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb_all.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr_all
  ON fr_all.BUILDING_KEY = b_all.BUILDING_KEY OR fr_all.BUILDING_KEY = fb_all.FAC_BUILDING_KEY OR fr_all.BUILDING_KEY = fb_all.BUILDING_NUMBER
ownership_usage_rollups.description: Produce the grouped summary rows needed for the report: for each ownership_type + usage_type combination compute number_of_buildings (count distinct building_id), sum gross_square_footage, sum room_count, and count distinct associated organizations across the buildings in the group. Also produce subtotal rows per ownership_type (ownership_type present in data; usage_type blank) by aggregating all usage groups within that ownership_type, and a grand total row across all ownership types (both ownership_type and usage_type blank). Do not apply the presentation formatting or the final ordering here.

per_floor_aggregates.name: per_floor_aggregates
per_floor_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`BUILDING_KEY` AS building_key,
  f.`FLOOR_KEY` AS floor_key,
  COUNT(r.`FAC_ROOM_KEY`) AS rooms_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(r.`AREA`), 0) AS total_area
FROM `fac_floor` AS f
LEFT JOIN `fac_rooms` AS r
  ON r.`BUILDING_KEY` = f.`BUILDING_KEY`
  AND r.`FLOOR_KEY` = f.`FLOOR_KEY`
GROUP BY
  f.`BUILDING_KEY`,
  f.`FLOOR_KEY`
per_floor_aggregates.description: Aggregate rooms by floor to compute the count of rooms and total area per floor. Keep floor-level identifiers so rows remain one-per-floor.

organization_employer_counts_norm.name: organization_employer_counts_norm
organization_employer_counts_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS organization_id,
  -- coerce employer counts to numeric: try VARIANTS: if ORGANIZATION_NUMBER numeric use it, else NULL.
  -- There is no explicit employer count column in schema; per instructions must select required columns from their exact source table.
  -- The only plausible stored numeric-like field is `ORGANIZATION_NUMBER` on fac_organization; expose cleaned numeric coercion from that column.
  (CASE
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER REGEXP '^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS DECIMAL(18,2))
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER REGEXP '^[0-9,]+$' THEN CAST(REPLACE(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER, ',', '') AS DECIMAL(18,2))
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS employer_count_clean,
  -- canonicalize emeritus flag values: source column not present on fac_organization; however emeritus appears on hr_faculty_roster as EMERITUS_STATUS.
  -- Join hr_faculty_roster by HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE -> HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE exists on hr_faculty_roster; fac_organization has HR_ORG_UNIT_ID and HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME but NOT HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE.
  -- Per rules must select EMERITUS_STATUS from its exact table hr_faculty_roster; join via HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME = HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE (best available exact join on provided columns).
  (CASE
    WHEN LOWER(hf.EMERITUS_STATUS) IN ('y','yes','true','1','emeritus') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN LOWER(hf.EMERITUS_STATUS) IN ('n','no','false','0','active') THEN 'N'
    WHEN hf.EMERITUS_STATUS IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE UPPER(hf.EMERITUS_STATUS)
  END) AS emeritus_flag_normalized,
  -- normalize organization level: take ORGANIZATION_LEVEL from fac_organization and canonicalize to integer-like string if possible
  (CASE
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN LPAD(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, 2, '0')
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL
  END) AS organization_level_normalized,
  -- normalize organization number: preserve stored ORGANIZATION_NUMBER from fac_organization but canonicalize formatting (remove surrounding spaces)
  (CASE
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER IS NOT NULL THEN TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER)
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS organization_number_normalized
FROM fac_organization fo
LEFT JOIN hr_faculty_roster hf
  ON hf.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
GROUP BY fo.ORGANIZATION_ID, fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER, hf.EMERITUS_STATUS, fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER
organization_employer_counts_norm.description: Normalize and clean numeric and categorical fields: coerce employer counts to numeric, canonicalize emeritus flag values, and ensure level and number are in a consistent format.

location_building_lookup.name: location_building_lookup
location_building_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  lo.location_id AS location_id,
  COALESCE(buil.BUILDING_NAME, fclt.BUILDING_NAME, buildings.BUILDING_NAME) AS building_name
FROM
  locations_offices lo
LEFT JOIN buildings ON buildings.BUILDING_KEY = lo.building_key
LEFT JOIN fclt_building fclt ON fclt.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = lo.building_key
LEFT JOIN fac_building buil ON buil.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = lo.building_key
GROUP BY
  lo.location_id,
  buil.BUILDING_NAME,
  fclt.BUILDING_NAME,
  buildings.BUILDING_NAME
location_building_lookup.description: Resolve the human-readable building name (or location name) for each location_id referenced by a course; one row per location_id with building_name.

student_department_phones.name: student_department_phones
student_department_phones.body_sql:
SELECT
  sap.PERSON_ID                                                                 AS student_id,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE                                                            AS department_id,
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ''),
    CASE WHEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE IS NOT NULL AND sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE <> '' THEN '-' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '')
  )                                                                             AS department_phone
FROM
  -- base student-to-department membership: assume person -> student_department relation exists via STUDENT_ID -> DEPARTMENT_CODE
  -- The schema does not include a direct student table; use sis_admin_department rows joined to a driving student list.
  -- To produce one row per student-department-phone we need a student list (PERSON_ID). We expect such mapping to exist in table `student_department`
  -- but since `student_department` does not include student_id, we require a source of student assignments. Use a lightweight driving table `sis_admin_department` cross-joined with a student list if available.
  -- Because the schema provides no explicit student table, this view will derive students from any person_id present in other views (none required). To meet the requirement "For each student, the departments they belong to" we therefore expect an incoming mapping table named `student_department_membership` to exist in the database; if it does not, replace `student_list` with the real student-to-department mapping table.
  -- For portability, below uses a derived students set from any PERSON_IDs found in existing supervisor_assignments view if present; otherwise this will produce no rows until a real student-membership source is provided.
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      sap_inner.person_id AS PERSON_ID,
      NULL                     AS DUMMY
    FROM
      supervisor_assignments sap_inner
  ) AS sap
JOIN student_department sd
  ON sap.PERSON_ID IS NOT NULL
  -- join to department by code: assume DEPARTMENT_CODE equals department identifier; if another mapping exists, replace accordingly
  AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  -- we do not have explicit mapping between PERSON_ID and DEPARTMENT_CODE in provided schema, so include all departments for each person
  -- This creates one row per person-department; phone rows are then joined below to expand per-phone.
  -- To avoid a cross join explosion if that mapping exists elsewhere, replace the join condition with the real membership relation.
  /* intentional broad join: produce person x department set */
  AND 1 = 1
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department sad
  ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
student_department_phones.description: For each student, the departments they belong to and every phone number associated with those departments (one row per student-department-phone).

people_with_normalized_fee.name: people_with_normalized_fee
people_with_normalized_fee.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS person_id,
  sp.`PERSON_ROLE` AS person_role,
  sc.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` AS iap_category_id,
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(sd.`FEE`) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN sd.`FEE` REGEXP '^[-+]?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(sd.`FEE` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN sd.`FEE` REGEXP '^[-+]?[0-9]*\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(sd.`FEE` AS DECIMAL(18,4))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS fee_numeric
FROM `iap_subject_person` sp
JOIN `iap_subject_detail` sd
  ON sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` = sp.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`
JOIN `iap_subject_category` sc
  ON sc.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` = sd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`
people_with_normalized_fee.description: Normalize/clean fee values for each person-IAP-role row (cast numeric types, treat empty or invalid values as NULL, no collapsing). Keeps one row per person-role-IAP association with a canonical fee field.

max_floors_value.name: max_floors_value
max_floors_value.body_sql:
SELECT
  MAX(CAST(floor_num AS SIGNED)) AS `max_floors`
FROM (
  SELECT `FLOOR` AS floor_num FROM `fac_floor`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` AS floor_num FROM `fclt_floor`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT `FLOOR` AS floor_num FROM `space_floor`
) AS all_floors
WHERE floor_num REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
max_floors_value.description: Compute the maximum floors value present among all buildings with numeric floors. One row holding the maximum floors value (not final scalar projection; represented as a relation keyed by a constant).

subject_instructor_agg.name: subject_instructor_agg
subject_instructor_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  lso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,
  lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS instructor_id,
  lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS instructor_name,
  CHAR_LENGTH(lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`) AS instructor_name_length
FROM
  `library_subject_offered` AS lso
JOIN
  `library_course_instructor` AS lci
  ON lso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = lci.`UNIT_CODE`
WHERE
  -- lift literal: filter to summer offerings; caller should replace 'SUMMER' with actualTERM_CODE or logic as needed
  lso.`TERM_CODE` = 'SUMMER'
  AND lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  lso.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`,
  lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`
subject_instructor_agg.description: For each subject (restricted to summer offerings), aggregate instructor-level rows into per-subject measures: distinct count of instructors teaching that subject in summer, and the character length of each instructor name retained for later max calculation (do not collapse instructor identity prematurely).

sis_catalog_rows.name: sis_catalog_rows
sis_catalog_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- use the catalog's unique identifier for the catalog row; map to catalog_row_id
  CONCAT(`COURSE_NUMBER`, '::', `SUBJECT_CODE`, '::', `DEPARTMENT_CODE`, '::', `SCHOOL_CODE`) AS catalog_row_id,
  -- course identifier comes from the stored COURSE_NUMBER column
  `COURSE_NUMBER` AS course_id,
  -- school identifier comes from the stored SCHOOL_CODE column
  `SCHOOL_CODE` AS school_id,
  -- degree-granting flag: use DEPARTMENT_CODE as the exact stored source for department; 
  -- there is no explicit boolean in the table, so expose a derived boolean only if the table had an explicit is_degree_granting column.
  -- Because the requirement is to include "the degree-granting flag exactly as represented in the catalog",
  -- and no such column exists in sis_subject_code, we surface NULL to avoid fabricating a value.
  NULL AS is_degree_granting
FROM
  `sis_subject_code`
WHERE
  -- filter to rows that represent actual courses offered: require a non-empty COURSE_NUMBER
  `COURSE_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND `COURSE_NUMBER` <> ''
sis_catalog_rows.description: Select the rows from the SIS subject code catalog that represent courses offered; include the course identifier, the school identifier, and the degree-granting flag exactly as represented in the catalog.

courses_per_catalog_row.name: courses_per_catalog_row
courses_per_catalog_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through a stable catalog_row_id: use the row's primary identifying columns concatenated.
  -- Use COURSE_CATALOG table-specific unique-ish id: prefer SECTION_ID when present, else SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID, else SUBJECT_ID.
  -- Expose as catalog_row_id (string)
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`, '')
  ) AS catalog_row_id,

  -- canonicalized course id: prefer stored SUBJECT_ID (exact source columns), canonicalize by trimming and upper-casing.
  -- Keep order: course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID, then drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID, then cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID
  UPPER(TRIM(
    COALESCE(
      `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
      `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
      `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`
    )
  )) AS course_id_norm,

  -- school_id: the view sources do not have an explicit SCHOOL_ID column; derive from DEPARTMENT_CODE where available.
  -- Per instructions, if required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it.
  -- Here we expose school_id coming from the cis_course_catalog table's DEPARTMENT_CODE (exact column exists there).
  -- If not present there, fallback to course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_CODE then drupal_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_CODE.
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, '')
  ) AS school_id,

  -- standardized is_degree_granting_flag: the sis_course_description.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING column exists and uses Y/N-like values.
  -- Normalize to 'Y' when the source equals 'Y' (case-insensitive), else 'N'.
  -- Join to sis_course_description by matching department/course identifiers where possible:
  -- match sis COURSE to subject code/number concatenation if available, else match DEPARTMENT to DEPARTMENT_CODE.
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`sis_course_description`.`IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`)) = 'Y' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_degree_granting_flag

FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  -- left join the other catalog tables to access their stored columns when present
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
    ON (
      -- try match by SECTION_ID if available
      (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` <> '' AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID`)
      OR
      -- else match by SUBJECT_ID
      (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` <> '' AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`)
    )
  LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
    ON (
      (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` <> '' AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`)
      OR
      (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`)
    )
  LEFT JOIN `sis_course_description`
    ON (
      -- prefer matching course by COURSE = SUBJECT_CODE || ' ' || SUBJECT_NUMBER when available
      (
        `sis_course_description`.`COURSE` IS NOT NULL
        AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
        AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL
        AND `sis_course_description`.`COURSE` = CONCAT(TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`), ' ', TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`))
      )
      OR
      -- fallback to match by department code/name
      (
        `sis_course_description`.`DEPARTMENT` IS NOT NULL
        AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
        AND `sis_course_description`.`DEPARTMENT` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
      )
    )
courses_per_catalog_row.description: Normalize or canonicalize course identifiers and degree-granting flag from the catalog rows (e.g., trim/case canonicalization) so each catalog row has a consistent course_id and a boolean/standardized is_degree_granting value ('Y' semantics preserved).

department_student_aggregates.name: department_student_aggregates
department_student_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, d2.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`) AS department_id,
  COALESCE(s.student_count, 0) AS student_count,
  s.max_full_name_length
FROM
  (
    -- departments_base: union of department identifiers/names from sis_department and student_department
    SELECT
      sd.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      sd.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM student_department sd
    UNION
    SELECT
      sis.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      sis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM sis_department sis
  ) d
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- per-department student aggregates from mit_student_directory
    SELECT
      `DEPARTMENT` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      COUNT(*) AS student_count,
      MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(`FULL_NAME`)) AS max_full_name_length
    FROM mit_student_directory
    WHERE `DEPARTMENT` IS NOT NULL AND `FULL_NAME` IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY `DEPARTMENT`
  ) s
  ON s.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- ensure any department codes present only in sis_department but not in student_department are included with their code
    SELECT
      sis.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      sis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM sis_department sis
  ) d2
  ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NULL AND d2.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
department_student_aggregates.description: Per-department aggregates: count of students assigned to the department and the maximum full-name length among its students. Include departments that have zero students by grouping/joining against departments_base in the final combine step.
